children: Shilpa Ranipeta Hyderabad: Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders (MDL) plans to invest about 15,000 crore in Andhra Pradesh over the next five to seven years to build a greenfield shipyard at Dugarajapatnam. The state-run shipbuilder inked a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with National Shipbuilding and Heavy Industries Park-AP (NSHIP-AP), a special purpose vehicle owned jointly by the Andhra Pradesh Maritime Board and Visakhapatnam Port Authority, for the facility.

The yard is expected to generate around 45,000 direct and indirect jobs and have an initial design capacity of 1.2 million gross tonnes (GT) a year. It will build commercial vessels including tankers, bulk carriers, container ships and LNG carriers. The project is part of Andhra Pradesh's proposed greenfield shipbuilding-cum-port cluster at Dugarajapatnam.

The state's techno-economic feasibility report estimates investment of 29,254 crore to develop the shipbuilding and ship-repair yard, and an additional 9,513 crore towards building a port. The shipbuilding cluster is being developed under the Centre's shipbuilding development scheme. The Andhra project follows MDL signing a MoU with the Tamil Nadu government in September 2025 to explore setting up a greenfield shipyard at Thoothukudi.

Tamil Nadu, however, picked South Korea's HD Korea Shipbuilding & Offshore Engineering as the anchor for this cluster. The Centre's current framework envisages one greenfield shipbuilding cluster per state, with Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu among the five to get in-principle approval. The Dugarajapatnam cluster has 3,488 acres and around 2.1 km of waterfront, while Thoothukudi has 2,050 acres and around 2.4 km of waterfront.

title: Mazagon Dock Plans to Invest 15k cr in Andhra Shipyard
